summary: Per-route weighting change during model rollout causing periodic 429 throttles for mixed realtime+batch traffic
description: Issue summary: After initiating a canary rollout from srd-large-v1.3 to srd-large-v1.4-quantized, the customer observed rhythmic 429 responses on specific low-latency routes used by their real-time inference pipeline. Impact: Up to 18% of realtime requests for the low-latency route returned 429 over 2-hour window; batch ingestion jobs experienced retries and backoff, causing downstream delays. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east backed by autoscaling group: dedicated-pool-342, per-route weightings enabled with custom weights for low-latency routes. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send mixed workload: steady realtime stream at 10 qps on route /v1/realtime-low-latency and a scheduled batch ingestion every 5 minutes. 2) Start canary rolling traffic 10% to new model variant with model pinning per rollout. 3) Observe 429s appear after model variant receives higher token-per-op counts. Logs & snippets: - Gateway logs show 429s with X-RateLimit-Remaining:0 and X-RateLimit-Window reset at 300s. - Serving runtime traces show new model variant increases average per-request token consumption ~2.7x due to longer prompt expansions. - Routing debug: per-route token-weight multiplier applied at admission leads to faster depletion of the tenant token bucket for that route.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: per-route weight multiplier combined with model variant's higher token consumption reduces effective tokens-per-window; autoscaler warmup/scale events introduce small throughput spikes and health-checks add probe traffic counted against same bucket. Confirmations: - Replayed traffic in staging with model variant reproduced the pattern. - Token bucket exhaustion coincides with the route's scheduled batch job start time (every 5m) + probe traffic causing sawtooth pattern. - Found route-level weight multiplier value (x3) configured for low-latency route which exaggerated impact of model variant token cost. Metrics referenced: request_token_rate, token_bucket_level, autoscaler_event_log, health_check_count. Cross-references: Slack #support-scribedata thread (https://slack.redwood/support-scribedata), PR to adjust rollout policy (https://github.com/redwood-inference/deployments/pull/4823), runbook: Confluence 'Rate limiting diagnostics' (https://confluence.redwood/rate-limits-runbook).
workaround: 1) Roll back the model rollout to 0% traffic for srd-large-v1.4-quantized for the affected customer. 2) Temporarily reduce per-route weight multiplier from x3 -> x1 for the low-latency route. 3) Schedule batch ingestion to stagger outside the 5-minute token window or apply a dedicated route with separate quota. These steps immediately reduced 429s in the customer's telemetry during tests.
next_steps: - Engineering to add a safeguard in the rollout controller to compute effective token-cost delta when promoting variants (owner: eng-rollouts). - Add optional per-route quota isolation toggle in dedicated pools so batch and realtime routes can have separate buckets (owner: product). - Short-term: propose automatic route-weight cap enforcement when model token cost exceeds baseline (follow-up PR linked). Target ETA for rollout-safeguard: 2026-03-20. Linked issues: ['SUP-71234','SUP-762318']
